content.comment_body: Hello, I have a question regarding programming with [product_name] Soft Comfort. When I check which type of [product_name] I can use, it only lists [article_no]. I keep getting messages like: Transmission PC --> [product_name] failed, device not suitable, block number too high. Is there a way to convert a program made for [article_no] to be compatible with [article_no]? Any advice would be appreciated. Regards

Hi, The [product_name] version [article_no] supports up to 130 function blocks, but your program uses blocks numbered 132 and 133, which exceed the limit. If you can reduce your block numbers below 130, it should work. The newer [product_name] version allows up to 200 blocks. Best regards,

Thank you for the quick reply! I'm new to this. How do I identify those blocks? I've uploaded the program as an attachment; maybe someone can look over it and point out where I'm going wrong. Thanks again!

Hello, Try using File -> Convert to FBD to display block numbers. At the bottom of your program, near Q5, you'll find many blocks numbered above 130. You'll need to renumber these blocks to 130 or lower. Best regards,

You can also upload your program here—just make a .ZIP file first. It's best to design your program using FBD; it's easier. Your program is quite large and not suitable for [article_no]. Upgrading to [article_no] is the best and most cost-effective option. It's unlikely you'll be able to recreate such a big program in just a few hours. With [article_no], you have up to 200 blocks to use, offering flexibility for tuning and additional features like text on the [product_name].

It's a problem if you don't have [article_no]. My advice, as mentioned by others, is to convert the code to FBD first, which makes finding block numbers easier. Then find blocks numbered above 130—preferably AND blocks. For example, if you find block number 142, create a new block of the same type with a number below 130, reconnect all inputs, and replace the output connections. Delete the old block once everything is transferred. Double-check your changes before deleting anything. It usually takes about 30–45 minutes. Check the attached photo. Good luck! By the way, this is probably the largest program I've seen built with [product_name].
All blocks used in the program can be viewed under block properties.

Hi, Here is the program modified to have block numbers below 130. Please verify its functionality. Steps: switch to FBD, locate the first block above 130, place a new block and connect it, then remove the block above 130. Hope this helps.

Hi [user_name], I'm not sure I understand. I see you changed the whole program, and block B130 is now the highest, with the rest under 130. When I select 'choose [product_name]', it shows the following stats: Function blocks 130/130, various device elements and limits. It lists [article_no], [article_no], and [article_no] as compatible versions. Can I upload this program to the [product_name], or do I need to do more work first? Thanks everyone for your speedy and informative responses!
Dear [user_name], The program is now compatible with [version_no] versions. Thanks to [user_name] for updating your program. You can now download it. Best regards,

Wow! I hope it works—I'm off work today and plan to try it tomorrow. Thanks so much to everyone for the helpful information, especially [user_name] for reprogramming! I'll report how it goes with the car tomorrow. Best regards!

analysis.insight_summary: The user was unable to transfer a program from a newer [product_name] module, which supports more function blocks, to an older version with a lower block limit. [product_name] Soft Comfort software indicated the program was too large. Other users explained the limitation, provided guidance on how to reduce block numbers, and eventually helped revise the program so it fits with the older device, resolving the compatibility issue.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hoped to easily run a program made for a newer [product_name] module on an older version without running into technical restrictions or needing complex troubleshooting.
